findings.explanation: The Splunk Universal Forwarder is not a Splunkbase app; it is downloaded from splunk.com, and splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404. The same false attribution is repeated in `app` and `detailedImplementation` Step 1, and it contradicts the HEC path named in `app` (HEC ingestion does not go through a forwarder).
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'Splunkbase 617' reference. Describe the real path: a custom scripted/REST input on a forwarder polling the VMS/ANPR server, or ANPR events pushed to an HTTP Event Collector token, writing sourcetype=cctv:analytics into index=physical. Name a vendor add-on only if one is confirmed on Splunkbase.

findings.explanation: A BMC EDAC (server memory-error) model has no relation to ANPR camera reads; the related `equipment` entry `hardware_bmc` is equally unrelated. This mis-routes the UC in equipment pickers.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `hardware_bmc_edac` (and `hardware_bmc` from equipment); map to CCTV/ANPR equipment only.

findings.explanation: Generic template: the SPL hard-codes earliest=-7d (overriding a -24h@h schedule), contains no macros or lookups (yet Step 4 routes 'from the lookup'), Step 3 compares an event count to a device inventory count, and Step 1 grants `list_inputs`/`search` 'on the target index' although capabilities are not index-scoped (index access comes from the role's allowed indexes). Nothing covers ANPR specifics such as plate-read fields or privacy controls.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite for this UC: how ANPR reads reach cctv:analytics (which `analytic_type` values, which plate field), a schedule matching the 7-day window or a report-style run, a restricted role for full plates, and validation against the ANPR system's read count for one camera.

findings.explanation: None of the scenarios names a real cause of misleading ANPR rows; the 'batch count ... without crossing configured threshold' item is not a false positive, and the SPL has no threshold.
findings.quote: **Synthetic probe on `plate`, `camera_id`, `action`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: OCR misreads splitting one vehicle into several plates, empty/unread plates grouped under an empty string, duplicate reads from overlapping cameras at the same gate, and test or fleet plates.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by 'catalog-team' while its prose is unedited template output and its collection path is wrong, so no SME review is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/unverified until an SME reviews the content.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no gate field; it groups by plate, camera_id and action only.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'reads per camera_id', or add a camera-to-gate lookup and document it.

findings.explanation: References are generic portal links shared by the whole subcategory; none documents ANPR event formats or the Splunk ingestion method used.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the vendor ANPR/LPR event API documentation and the Splunk HEC or scripted-input documentation actually used.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Title promises an 'Event Audit Trail' but the SPL aggregates seven days into `stats count by plate camera_id action`, discarding per-read timestamps; `coalesce(license_plate, plate_text, "")` also lumps all unread plates into one empty-string row. An audit trail needs per-read rows (_time, plate, camera_id, action) or at least first/last seen.

summary: Almost every prose field is cross-UC template residue; only the short implementation and visualization lines are about ANPR. The collection path attributes the Universal Forwarder to a non-existent Splunkbase app, and the equipment model mapping (BMC EDAC) has nothing to do with licence-plate recognition.
